item.title: Dan Campbell: We won't accept mediocrity on either side of the ball
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Saints knocked the Lions out of the top spot for points allowed on Monday night, but being anywhere near the top of that list is not where teams want to be four weeks into the season.
item.content:encoded:
The Saints knocked the Lions out of the top spot for points allowed on Monday night, but being anywhere near the top of that list is not where teams want to be four weeks into the season.

Detroit has allowed at least 24 points and 355 yards in each of their four games, which led to head coach Dan Campbell's vote of confidence for defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard after Sunday night's loss to the Panthers. During an appearance on 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday, Campbell pointed to a lack of discipline and a lack of trust among players on the unit as reasons why the defense has been so easily torn apart. He added that others will get opportunities as the team looks for the right mix to improve their results.

"We’re going to give some other guys an opportunity, and go, man. But we’re not going to accept mediocrity. That’s not what we’re doing here," Campbell said. "We've got too many guys playing at a high level, and we’re going to raise the floor on this team."

The Lions offense ranks fifth in the league in points scored, but some have wondered if the defense's inability to get stops has an adverse effect on the offense. Campbell was asked about that, but said he thinks the team has been "average" across the board and that the offense has room to improve alongside the defense.

"Man, if you want to be great, they should want to score 35 points a game, at a minimum," Campbell said. "That’s what greatness is. That’s what they’re charged with. We've got plenty of weapons on offense and if we’re gonna accept mediocrity, then yeah, we can make all the excuses in the world. If we want to spit and sputter and be average, that’s one thing. We’re not going to be average. We’re going to raise the floor on these guys, man. We’re going to push ‘em. We've got too much offensively right now. Our quarterback’s too good, our playmakers are too good, and we've got a young, hungry offensive line that’s got a ton of room to grow."

Campbell was adamant this summer that the Lions' Super Bowl window is not closed, but the first four weeks haven't done much to support the feeling that big things are in store for the team this season. That will need to change quickly if they want to avoid calls for more sweeping changes to how business is getting done in Detroit.

item.title: NFL was right to hold officials to a higher standard than coaches, players
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Monday, the NFL did what it needed to do, as to a pair of officials who failed to act the way officials should act.
item.content:encoded:
On Monday, the NFL did what it needed to do, as to a pair of officials who failed to act the way officials should act.

Line judge Jeff Seeman was suspended two games for his double-F-bomb directed to Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. Referee Adrian Hill received a one-game suspension for his overreactive interaction with Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson after Wilson accidentally knocked Hill to the ground.

Hill may not have been suspended without the Jeff Seeman incident. Hill didn't know why or how he got knocked down. He reacted to a misimpression of the situation.

And for good reason. Last year, Hill suffered a non-contact leg injury during a Thursday night game between the Bills and Texans. He's surely sensitive to the possibility of getting injured again.

The NFL Players Association, which objected to the Seeman incident with a strong statement from executive director JC Tretter, had nothing to say about the Hill-Wilson exchange.

Regardless, the league took action as to both Seeman and Hill. The league had no choice. The officials are supposed to be neutral, measured, and detached. They're the judges in the courtroom that is a football field. And judges typically don't say "fuck you" to the lawyers or the parties who appear before them. (A judge or two may have wanted to say it to me during my former career, but never did. At least not loud enough for me to hear it.)

Appearances matter. How can anyone expect the players and coaches to restrict their behavior if the officials can't, or won't?

Besides, the NFL has suddenly gone fine-happy over previously acceptable celebrations by players. Also, it's constantly looking for any type of actual or perceived "taunting" indignity that could increase the on-field temperature between players. That standard should apply to officials — and it should be an even higher bar.

The league has proven that it is. And that it will.

item.title: Steelers bring KJ Henry back to their practice squad
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: For the third time in the last 12 months, pass rusher KJ Henry has signed with the Steelers.
item.content:encoded:
For the third time in the last 12 months, pass rusher KJ Henry has signed with the Steelers.

Henry is signing to Pittsburgh's practice squad, according to Mike Garafolo.

The Steelers also signed Henry to their practice squad on October 11 of last year, and then after he ended last season on the Browns' practice squad, the Steelers re-signed him to a futures contract in January before cutting him in June.

Now that defensive lineman Derrick Harmon has gone on injured reserve, the Steelers need more depth in their defensive front, and so Henry is back for a third time.

Henry originally arrived in the NFL as a fifth-round pick of the Commanders out of Clemson in 2023. He has also spent time with the Bengals, Cowboys, Eagles and 49ers. He has played in 15 games in his NFL career and recorded 2.5 sacks.

item.title: Bijan Robinson, Kenneth Walker III should be serious MVP candidates
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The MVP award has become, essentially, a "best quarterback" award — with rare exceptions.
item.content:encoded:
The MVP award has become, essentially, a "best quarterback" award — with rare exceptions.

No non-quarterback has won the MVP prize since Vikings running back Adrian Peterson eked out the distinction over Peyton Manning in 2012. In the current century, a non-quarterback became the MVP only four times: Marshall Faulk in 2000, Shaun Alexander in 2005, LaDainian Tomlinson in 2006, and Peterson in 2012.

This year, a couple of running backs deserve serious consideration, based on what we've seen through four weeks.

Falcons running back Bijan Robinson is a touchdown waiting to happen, on any given play. His opening-drive 59-yard touchdown run on Monday night in New Orleans set the tone for Atlantas' 45-24 win.

Though four games, Robinson has 494 yards rushing and 120 yards receiving and five total touchdowns.

Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III has become the straw that stirs the Kansas City cocktail. He has 537 yards rushing, 84 yards receiving, and six total touchdowns. He's also the third player in NFL history to have 170 or more rushing yards in two of the first four games of a season, joining only Jim Brown and O.J. Simpson.

Both Robinson and Walker have 99 touches. Walker has gained 621 yards. Robinson has gained 614.

When it comes to the MVP betting odds (which are instructive to the general perceptions that surely will influence some or many of the 50 Associated Press voters), both Robinson and Walker are low on the list. Robinson, who was 70-1 when Simms and I discussed the dynamic earlier this morning on PFT Live, is now at 60-1. Walker is 50-1.

Currently, the eight highest players on the list of odds are quarterbacks.

Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs sits at 30-1, which may be a reflection of the bets made on him before the season started. (He has 102 touches and 540 yards from scrimmage, with seven touchdowns.)

Here's the real question. Is the perception of "value" skewed by the fact that the best quarterbacks make so much more money than the best quarterbacks? The top of the quarterback market is approaching $65 million per year. Gibbs, the highest-paid running back, is at $22.5 million annually.

Robinson sits at $22.25 million per year. Walker, who signed as a free agent months before the Robinson and Gibbs deals were done, is making $14.35 million per year. (To put it apples-to-apples terms, the Gibbs deal is worth $16.995 million per year from signing, Robinson’s deal has an average of $16.36 million from signing.)

The best running backs are far more valuable to their teams than the market suggests. The existing market held back Walker, Robinson, and Gibbs. The enhanced injury risk at the position is a major factor in the unwillingness of teams to embrace the financial risk that the player at some point won't be available.

While their "value" may not properly be reflected in their contracts, it needs to be recognized in their consideration for the MVP award. The present betting trends show that it's not. Whether it will be comes down to the ability and willingness of the voters to stop viewing the MVP as a quarterback prize and to start looking at the definition of the prize, as articulated by the AP.

"The player who was most valuable to their team over the course of the season."

Robinson and Walker fit the bill. Gibbs will, too, if the Lions can recover from a sluggish start and become true contenders.

item.title: Sean McVay says Rams' coaches need to "get the hell out of the way" after sideline penalty
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Rams quarterbacks coach Dave Ragone got a 15-yard penalty for unsportsmanlike conduct on Sunday after he stood too close to the field and collided with an official who was running down the sideline.
item.content:encoded:
Rams quarterbacks coach Dave Ragone got a 15-yard penalty for unsportsmanlike conduct on Sunday after he stood too close to the field and collided with an official who was running down the sideline. Rams coach Sean McVay says that can't happen.

When talking about some of the mistakes the Rams made in the first three quarters before turning things around and beating the Eagles with a fourth-quarter comeback, McVay noted that the coaches aren't exempt from the criticism that the team hasn't been focused enough at times.

"Focus, concentration and situational awareness, we have to do a better job on that," McVay said. "When it rains, it pours. Shoot, we’re getting penalties on our staff now too. Thank God we won that one. Rags would have never lived that one down. He felt bad about that one. So he took great accountability. We'll get everybody the hell out of the way. And I need to get the hell out of the way as well.”

It was one of several costly penalties for the Rams, who were flagged eight times for 100 penalty yards. They won the game, but McVay wants to make sure everyone, players and coaches alike, knows that can't happen.

item.title: Sean McVay: Myles Garrett is "making really good progress," no word on when he'll play
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Rams defensive end Myles Garrett has to be on injured reserve for at least one more week.
item.content:encoded:
Rams defensive end Myles Garrett has to be on injured reserve for at least one more week. The Rams aren't sure whether he'll return after that.

Coach Sean McVay said that Garrett is coming along in his rehab from knee surgery but McVay doesn't know how many more games Garrett might miss.

"I know he's making really good progress. We haven't talked specifics like that," McVay said.

McVay said he and Reggie Scott, who runs the team's sports medicine department, will review Garrett's rehab this week and will have a better idea of Garrett's timeline soon.

"That'll be something that I talk with Reggie about in the next couple days," McVay said. "Probably be better equipped to give you some clarity about that on Thursday."

Garrett struggled to play through his knee injury in Week 1 and hasn't played since, which is a big disappointment for such an important offseason acquisition. But the most important thing is getting Garrett healthy now, and having the Garrett of old on the field down the stretch.

item.title: NFL suspends referee Adrian Hill, line judge Jeff Seeman for unprofessional conduct toward players
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Hill has been suspended for one game while Seeman received a two-game ban
item.content:encoded:
The NFL has issued a pair of suspensions to officials after incidents with players during Sunday's games.

The league has suspended referee Adrian Hill one game and line judge Jeff Seeman for two games for unprofessional conduct. The suspensions were issued by NFL vice president of officiating Ramon George.

Hill was knocked over by Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson while Wilson was being blocked by Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon through the whistle. Hill got up and got in Wilson's face while yelling at him to get back to his team's huddle. Wilson was not penalized on the play.

Cameras caught Seeman saying "f—k you" twice to Cardinals tight end Trey McBride after McBride complained about the lack of a flag for pass interference during Arizona's loss to the Giants. The NFL Players Association called Seeman's response "unacceptable" in a statement to PFT on Sunday.

item.title: Mike McCarthy, Aaron Rodgers talked "numerous times" after Thursday night's heated exchange
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Week 4 began with Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and coach Mike McCarthy exchanging unpleasantries for all the world to see, and hear.
item.content:encoded:
Week 4 began with Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and coach Mike McCarthy exchanging unpleasantries for all the world to see, and hear.

Rodgers looked to McCarthy while waiting for a play call. A Prime Video microphone captured Rodgers angrily yelling, “What the fuck? Call it!”

McCarthy was then seen mouthing his response: “Fucking asshole.”

After the game, McCarthy was asked about the interaction; Rodgers was not. On Monday, the situation came up multiple times again during a McCarthy press conference in advance of the Week 5 game against the Colts.

"I wouldn't classify it as normal," McCarthy said of the interaction, "but I think the reality of it is, you know, it's a 20-year relationship. I think the fact that we were able to sit and talk numerous times, you know, over the weekend, about that and a number of things.

"As I stated, I'm — hopefully, not to put any pressure on my daughter — I'm getting to grandfather age. You know, I don't want to be saying those type of words. But it's an emotional, competitive environment. I think it's something that we can definitely learn from."

McCarthy also was asked whether the game broadcasts have become too intrusive.

"Your question's about 15 years too late," McCarthy said.

Earlier in the press conference, McCarthy said he had told the team on Thursday morning that it would be important to play the Browns with "more emotion."

He wanted it, and he got it.

"With that comes the discipline of it," McCarthy said. "So I think those are opportunities for growth. But I'd much rather have too much energy than not enough."

Amen to that. It's always easier to try to control enthusiasm than to create it when it's not there. On Thursday night, however, it became a little too unbridled.

Come Wednesday, Rodgers will have a chance to respond. Unless he decides to call McAfee's show on Tuesday and air any grievances he may have about the incident, how it was covered by the media, and anything else he chooses to publicly gripe about.

item.title: Bengals call Tee Higgins day-to-day with adductor injury
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bengals saw their top two receivers leave Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jaguars with injuries and it's unclear if either one of them will be back for Week 5.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals saw their top two receivers leave Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jaguars with injuries and it's unclear if either one of them will be back for Week 5.

Head coach Zac Taylor told reporters on Monday that Tee Higgins is considered day-to-day after suffering an adductor injury late in Sunday's game. Higgins had 11 catches for 157 yards before his injury.

One of the reasons that Higgins saw so many targets was the absence of Ja'Marr Chase, who left the game in the second quarter. Chase has been diagnosed with a concussion and will need to clear concussion protocol before he will be able to return to action.

The 2-2 Bengals will be in Miami next weekend and they have a bye in Week 6.

item.title: Colts DE Arden Key to miss time with hamstring injury
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Colts won't have defensive end Arden Key in the lineup for a while.
item.content:encoded:
The Colts won't have defensive end Arden Key in the lineup for a while.

Key injured his hamstring in Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders in London and head coach Shane Steichen said at a Monday press conference that Key is going to miss more time moving forward. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that Key is expected to miss three or four weeks.

That timeline could make Key a candidate for injured reserve, which would mean he'd miss at least four games. The Colts play the Steelers, Titans, Vikings and Jaguars in the next four weeks.

Key has eight tackles, a half-sack and a forced fumble so far this season.

Why one member of Chicago’s dynamic rushing attack suffered an injury on Sunday, it may not keep him sidelined for long — if at all.

“We think he's going to be OK,” Johnson said, via transcript from the team. “We'll see what it looks like as we go through the week here, but more of a day-to-day type deal.”

While D’Andre Swift is Chicago’s starter, Monangai leads the team with 324 yards rushing, averaging 5.4 yards per carry. Swift has 311 yards, averaging 4.5 yards per carry.

item.title: Jessie Bates: We're a different team with Michael Penix in the lineup
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: During the first two weeks of the 2026 season, the Falcons looked like one of the worst teams in the NFL.
item.content:encoded:
During the first two weeks of the 2026 season, the Falcons looked like one of the worst teams in the NFL.

The last two weeks have been much different. A 35-14 win in Green Bay in Week 3 was followed by Monday night's 45-24 rout of the Saints in New Orleans and it's not hard to notice the biggest difference in the team over the last two games. Quarterback Michael Penix was cleared to return from last season's torn ACL and he's been at the helm of their offensive explosion.

Penix is 33-of-45 for 479 yards and two touchdowns in the two wins and combining accuracy with an ability to pick up big chunks of yardage every time the ball is in the air has opened the door for the Falcons to run wild. Bijan Robinson has run for 339 yards and four touchdowns while Brian Robinson has 117 yards to go with four more scores in the back-to-back wins. The change in offense has made a strong impression on safety Jessie Bates.

"We just want to show the world who we can be," Bates said, via Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com. "The first two weeks were not up to our standards. Obviously, when you got [Penix] back there dealing, it's a whole different team. So, we're just excited to continue to go with this."

The Falcons had a strong collection of skill position players to open the season, but poor quarterback play didn't allow them to take advantage of that talent. The shift with Penix has been clear and it's opened the door to a much brighter future in Atlanta.

item.title: Report: "Outside chance" Lamar Jackson plays in Week 5
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Tyler Huntley would start for the Ravens if Jackson is out.
item.content:encoded:
Signs continue to point toward Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson missing Sunday night's game in Atlanta.

PFT reported that Jackson was considered week-to-week after injuring his ankle in Baltimore's Week 4 win over the Titans with an MRI still to come to determine the extent of the issue. Jackson underwent further evaluation on Monday and Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that there is only an "outside chance" that he will be available against the Falcons.

Jackson's chances of playing in Week 6 will rely on how his sprained ankle responds to treatment.

Tyler Huntley will start for the Ravens as long as Jackson is out of action. Huntley was 8-of-9 for 63 yards in the second half of the win over the Titans and he has started 11 times for Baltimore over the years. He also made five starts for the Dolphins in 2024.

item.title: Drew Rosenhaus: Tyreek Hill could sign with a team this week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: A return to the Chiefs could be in the cards for the wide receiver.
item.content:encoded:
Wide receiver Tyreek Hill could be back in the NFL very soon.

Hill's agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN that he plans to begin negotiations with teams about a contract for the wideout. Rosenhaus added that he does not expect it to take a long time for those talks to lead to an agreement.

“I would anticipate Tyreek potentially signing with a team over the next few days,” Rosenhaus said.

One of the teams that Rosenhaus is expected to be talking to is the Chiefs. Word on Sunday was that they have already reached out to show their interest in a reunion with Hill and their urgency to get something done went up when Tyquan Thornton dislocated his ankle during Sunday's win over the Raiders.

Hill spent his first six seasons with the Chiefs and was a three-time first-team All-Pro while helping the team win the first of three Super Bowls under head coach Andy Reid. He was traded to Miami ahead of the 2022 season, but could be back with the Chiefs in the near future.

item.title: Former Bears LB Otis Wilson had altercation with security at Soldier Field
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Sunday's Jets-Bears game has an unexpected postscript.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday's Jets-Bears game has an unexpected postscript.

Via Kalyn Kahler of ESPN, former Bears linebacker Otis Wilson was involved in an altercation with multiple security officers at Soldier Field.

Wilson, a member of the legendary 1985 Bears Super Bowl championship team, reportedly boarded a media elevator. An argument ensued, resulting in conflicting allegations from Wilson and the security personnel.

Wilson claims that he and his wife were "assaulted by private security personnel." The security company claims that Wilson "forced his way onto the elevator," became "physically combative and violently attacked" a female officer, and "aggressively threw the female officer into a wall . . . leaving a large hole in the wall."

Wilson said he was taken by ambulance to a local hospital, where he was treated and released. The security company claims that the female officer was also transported to a hospital with "substantial bruising and injuries to her ribs and arms."

As Kahler explains it, multiple reporters witnessed the moments before the incident. Wilson and his wife boarded an elevator meant for the media. Wilson and his wife were asked to leave. They refused. Security personnel then tried to physically remove them.

Wilson has asked Soldier Field and the security company to "preserve all surveillance and body camera footage of the incident, to conduct a full and transparent investigation, and to hold the individuals responsible accountable."

David Haugh of 104.3 The Score in Chicago witnessed the incident, and he discussed it during the Monday edition of his show.

"It was an ugly sight," Haugh said. "There was a hole in the wall" where the incident occurred.

"There's got to be a better way to expedite this whole situation," Haugh said regarding the practice of making an elevator available only to the media, at a time when others are also trying to leave the stadium.

He's right. And, at a minimum, there's a point at which someone who technically shouldn't be on the elevator should be allowed to ride it down without a fight happening. The security officers seemingly were too zealous when it came to getting Wilson and his wife out of the elevator. Wilson, based on the security company's statement, overreacted, and it cascaded.

We've got a feeling that the available visual evidence will show that both sides carry blame for this one. Which could mean that Wilson and one or more security officers could be facing legal consequences, once the situation is fully sorted out.

Moving forward, and as Haugh said, there has to be a better way to ensure that the media can get to the locker room to do their work after a game, without chaos unfolding.

item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Injuries be damned, the 49ers have risen to the top.
item.content:encoded:
1. 49ers (last week No. 3; 4-0): Take that, substation.

2. Chiefs (No. 2; 4-0): They need help at receiver, badly.

3. Jaguars (No. 5; 3-1): The Jaguars have the best shot at winning the No. 1 seed in the AFC.

4. Bills (No. 1; 3-1): The benefited from getting early-season wins against teams that aren't as good as most thought they'd be.

5. Seahawks (No. 6; 3-1): Let Rashid cook.

6. Broncos (No. 4; 2-2): The Davis Webb problem isn't going away.

7. Rams (No. 8; 2-2): It shouldn't have been as hard as it was in Philly.

8. Vikings (No. 9; 4-0): Kyler Murray is no longer the Road Runner.

9. Bears (No. 10; 3-1): Kyle Monangai may be emerging as the best tailback option.

10. Ravens (No. 12; 3-1): They'll need Lamar Jackson back sooner than later.

11. Raiders (No. 15; 3-1): Even though they lost, the Raiders must be regarded as a contender.

12. Browns (No. 18; 3-1): The Browns may soon be saying, "The Steelers is the Steelers."

13. Patriots (No. 20; 2-2): Drake Maye was under more pressure than anyone in Week 4, and he delivered.

14. Steelers (No. 13; 2-2): The best-case scenario is 9-8. The worst-case scenario is they're giving Will Howard or Drew Allar game reps after Thanksgiving.

15. Bengals (No. 7; 2-2): The Super Bowl pipe dream is quickly imploding.

16. Giants (No. 16; 3-1): Giants fans will age like presidents with Jameis Winston playing quarterback.

17. Eagles (No. 11; 2-2): It's quickly getting very ugly in Philly.

18. Cowboys (No. 21; 2-2): They have a chance to start stacking wins, until the 49ers come to town in Week 10.

19. Panthers (No. 26; 2-2): Bryce Young is getting better and better all the time.

20. Falcons (No. 22; 2-2): Just give the ball to a Robinson on every play.

21. Lions (No. 14; 2-2): The Super Bowl window sure seems closed.

22. Colts (No. 24; 2-2): Can they win enough games to steal a wild-card berth?

23. Packers (No. 25; 2-2): It never felt like they truly wanted to beat the Buccaneers.

24. Texans (No. 17; 0-4): Where did the Houston defense go?

25. Saints (No. 19; 1-3): They've improved, but not nearly enough to contend.

26. Commanders (No. 23; 1-3): It's getting late early for the Commanders and coach Dan Quinn.

27. Cardinals (No. 27; 1-3): With each Chargers' loss, the Week 1 win looks less impressive.

28. Jets (No. 28; 1-3): Woody Johnson may soon be tempted to let Mike Tomlin build Minecraft Manhattan.

29. Chargers (No. 29; 0-4): Andrew Luck retired and stopped playing. Justin Herbert has apparently retired and kept playing.

30. Buccaneers (No. 30; 0-4): It could get very ugly on Thursday night in Dallas.

31. Titans (No. 31; 0-4): They're getting a new stadium. One of these days, they'll get a new team.

32. Dolphins (No. 32; 0-4): Could the first team to go 17-0 go 0-17?

item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Eagles have a problem at running back.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles have a problem at running back.

Starting tailback Saquon Barkley suffered a hamstring injury on his first and only carry of Sunday's loss to the Rams. He didn't return.

Via NFL Network, Barkley is "week-to-week." Which is worse than "day-to-day," and implies he'll miss at least one week.

There has been no reporting on the degree of the hamstring strain. Whatever the extent of the damage, it's an injury that takes time to heal.

Time is of the essence for the Eagles. They play the Jaguars in London on Sunday. And Tank Bigsby is out with core muscle surgery.

That leaves Ryan Shipley as the starter, barring a roster move. Jaydon Blue, Dameon Pierce, and Carson Steele are on the practice squad.

A trade is possible, in theory. Desperation, however, will drive up the price. The Eagles also could scour the other practice squads in search of someone who may want to make the jump to Philly and fill in while Barkley is out.

item.title: Falcons average NFL-high 40.0 points with Michael Penix, after NFL-low 8.0 without him
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Falcons safety Jessie Bates wasn't exaggerating when he said they're a different team with Michael Penix.
item.content:encoded:
Falcons safety Jessie Bates wasn't exaggerating when he said they're a different team with Michael Penix.

After starting the season 0-2, the Falcons are 2-0 since Penix became the starter in Week 3. But even that doesn't fully display how different things have been with Penix.

On average, NFL teams are scoring 23.1 points per game this season. If we considered the Falcons two different teams, with Penix and without him, the version with Penix would rank first in the NFL with an average of 40.0 points per game — more than a touchdown better than the No. 1, the Bills, who average 31.8 points per game. Meanwhile, the version of the Falcons without Penix averaged 8.0 points per game. That ranks dead last, more than a field goal worse than the No. 32 Dolphins, who are averaging 11.5 points per game.

Among the 42 quarterbacks who have thrown at least 15 passes this season, Penix ranks fifth with a 113.1 passer rating. The two Falcons quarterbacks who played before Penix are dead last: Rush ranks 41st with a 42.5 passer rating, and Jack Strand ranks 42nd with a 35.1 passer rating.

How much better is Penix at avoiding pressure than Rush and Strand? Rush was sacked five times while throwing 39 passes. Strand was sacked twice while throwing 15 passes. Penix has been sacked only once while throwing 45 passes, and Penix played most of the second game after the Falcons lost starting left tackle Jake Matthews to an injury.

The effect of Penix on his teammates is notable. In two games with Penix, Falcons running back Bijan Robinson has rushed for 339 yards and four touchdowns. In two games without Penix, Robinson rushed for 155 yards and no touchdowns. Backup running back Brian Robinson has 24 carries for 112 yards and four touchdowns with Penix. He had 20 carries for 82 yards and no touchdowns without Penix.

The Falcons' top receiver, Drake London, has 14 catches for 290 yards in two games with Penix. London had six catches for 80 yards in two games without Penix.

That stats are a remarkable display of just how well Penix is playing — and just how poorly Rush and Strand played. With a different quarterback, the Falcons are a completely different team.

item.title: Matt LaFleur explains his reason for not taking the bait from Ben Johnson
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Bears coach Ben Johnson has no qualms about making his disdain for the Packers known.
item.content:encoded:
Bears coach Ben Johnson has no qualms about making his disdain for the Packers known. Green Bay coach Matt LaFleur takes a different approach to the situation.

LaFleur explained his decision not to take Ben Johnson's bait to reporters on Monday.

“Because this game is about players and so we’ll keep it about the players," LaFleur said, via Matt Schneidman of The Athletic. "I’m not the one out there they’re playing. . . . Don’t get me wrong. I love the rivalry. It’s awesome. It’s great. It’s intense. You can feel it on gameday. You can feel it throughout the course of the week and also the significance, I mean, they’re the defending [NFC] North champions. So what a great opportunity, great challenge for us in our home stadium to play against the defending champs.”

For Johnson's part, he sent a clear message to his players about Sunday's game at Lambeau Field.

"He wants to beat them really bad like everyone else in the room, like every Chicago fan. Beat them real bad, and make them quit," receiver Luther Burden III said, via Cassie Carlson of Fox32.

Johnson's anti-Green Bay antics have included declaring in the locker room after a playoff win, "Fuck the Packers! Fuck them!"

"The Bears and the Packers, they should not like each other," Johnson said in a Scouting Combine-week appearance on PFT Live. "I think it's as simple as that. And I think that's gonna make this rivalry, this game, something that people are going to watch here going forward."

For fans, that's absolutely true. Players and coaches are interchangeable. Coaches can be nomads, hopping from job to job regardless of where the job may be. And they generally refrain from making things personal because today's enemy could be tomorrow's employer.

Johnson, to his credit, isn't willing to play the game. He earned his stripes with the Packers as a rival (Johnson and the Lions spoiled Aaron Rodgers's last game in Green Bay), and he's in position to be the coach of the Bears for a long time. He could become as beloved as Mike Ditka, in time.

He's off to a good start. In part because he says what most Bears fans believe about the Packers.

As to this weekend's game, which was moved out of the higher-profile 4:25 p.m. ET window for 1:00 p.m. ET, Johnson surely will say, privately and/or publicly, that the flex didn't happen because of the Bears but because (as Johnson is more likely to say privately but who knows?), "The Packers suck."

item.title: Kellen Moore: Really disappointing how Saints played on an incredible night in New Orleans
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: On the 20th anniversary of the Saints' return to New Orleans following Hurricane Katrina, it was the Falcons who had a big game.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL scheduled the Saints to host the Falcons on Monday night to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the Superdome's reopening after Hurricane Katrina. It was a big night in New Orleans, and the Saints did not match the fans' energy.

Saints head coach Kellen Moore said after the 45-24 loss that the team came out flat despite the excitement of the moment.

"Really disappointing game for us," Moore said. "The dome was an incredible night, incredible energy. I did a poor job preparing our football team. Didn't coach well enough, didn't play well enough. It wasn't good enough. We're at where we're at, a 1-3 football team with some good moments but not enough consistent football to be where we ultimately want to be. We've got a lot of work to do."

Moore said he addressed the historical significance of the game with his team and thought they bought into this being a particularly big game. But when it was time to put it all together, they didn't.

"We talked about it at the beginning of the week, the guys were fired up," Moore said. "I thought there was good energy, we just didn't execute well enough."

The Saints saw the nationally televised, much-discussed game as a big opportunity to show what kind of team they are, and they didn't show much.

"Those are big-time opportunities," Moore said. "It's just disappointing for us and I know there's frustration for everyone."

item.title: Klint Kubiak: I put Raiders' problems running the ball on myself
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Raiders opened the season with 130 rushing yards in a win over the Dolphins and that was a welcome development after the team finished dead last in rushing during the 2025 season.
item.content:encoded:
The Raiders opened the season with 130 rushing yards in a win over the Dolphins and that was a welcome development after the team finished dead last in rushing during the 2025 season.

The past three weeks have suggested that might have had more to do with the opponent than anything the Raiders have done to change their scheme or personnel. They've run for 242 yards in those games, which isn't as bad as they were last season but it's also not where head coach Klint Kubiak would like things to be in Las Vegas.

Among the issues is that Raiders backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington are averaging just 1.8 yards before contact and Kubiak said he isn't looking at anyone else when it comes to finding ways to "scheme them up better."

“I put it on myself," Kubiak said on Monday. "I got to do a lot better job of putting us in better position. We’ve got solid backs, we’ve got a solid offensive line. Myself and the coaching staff, there’s plenty of things we can do better for our players.”

A 3-0 start helped downplay any concerns about the way the Raiders have been playing, but Sunday's loss to the Chiefs put the lagging run game in greater focus and it will continue to be one if a three-game run against the Patriots, Bills and Rams does not go well for Kubiak's side.

item.title: Tyler Shough: Fans are understandably upset, I'd boo too
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Monday night's game in New Orleans started with a tribute to a storybook night in Saints history, but there was no happily ever after once the game got underway.
item.content:encoded:
Monday night's game in New Orleans started with a tribute to a storybook night in Saints history, but there was no happily ever after once the game got underway.

Falcons running back Bijan Robinson broke loose for a 59-yard touchdown a few plays into the game that took some life out of the Superdome crowd. The Saints weren't able to stop the bleeding and the Falcons rolled to a 45-24 win that left the Superdome crowd feeling much differently than they did at the outset.

Cheers for the 20th anniversary of the Saints' return to New Orleans after Hurricane Katrina were replaced by cascades of boos until enough Saints fans left the building that Falcons supporters had run of the place. The loss dropped the Saints to 1-3 and quarterback Tyler Shough could not take any issue with the way that the home crowd responded to the effort.

"Fans understandably are upset," Shough said. "We had some opportunities that we didn't take advantage of and you're playing the Falcons and you lose like that? I mean, I'd boo, too. That sucks. We want to get everybody going. It’s part of it. You have to have the energy of the crowd and we’re gonna need them next week too against a really good team. That’s the best part about New Orleans. You feel it and we feel it too, and we’re gonna keep going."

A 4-1 close to last season with Shough playing well led to hopes of a turnaround for a team that hasn't been to the playoffs since 2020, but the Saints have allowed the most points in the league through four weeks. They have two of their next three games at home before a bye week and they'll need to plug a lot of leaks in order to ensure no one will be considering a return to paper bags on heads later in this year's home schedule.

item.title: Jim Harbaugh not happy with reporter for "more insult than question" about Justin Herbert
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh was not happy with a reporter's line of questioning about quarterback Justin Herbert and the Chargers' inability to build a successful offense around him amid the team's 0-4 start.
item.content:encoded:
Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh was not happy with a reporter's line of questioning about quarterback Justin Herbert and the Chargers' inability to build a successful offense around him amid the team's 0-4 start.

At his Monday press conference, Harbaugh responded to a question from reporter Kris Rhim of ESPN by saying Rhim had delivered an insult, not asked a question. Harbaugh had previously praised Herbert for how tough he was continuing to play on Sunday after taking some hard hits, and Rhim questioned why the Chargers' offense hasn't been able to better protect Herbert so he doesn't take so many hard hits. That led to this exchange:

Rhim: "Jim, when you talk about he's a warrior, he's gritty, part of that is just him taking a ruthless beating because of, I don't know if it's the group in front of him, his protection, what's going on, but when you came here, your charge was to get him protected. Mike's [McDaniel] charge was to make sure he didn't have to be a superhero, but 2.5 years later, like you said, he still has to be a superhero for you guys to have a chance to win the game. Why is that?"

Harbaugh: "Yeah, that just sounds more like an insult than it does a question, but if that's the way you look at it. I'm saying that it's the kind of competitor that he is where I've never seen him flinch. I've never seen him rattled. He's an amazing inspiration and that's what we do. We all feed off of that. I know the entire team does. And you ask me what gives me optimism, what gives me hope with this football team, because I see that throughout the entire team. And yeah, we attack, we improve, can't improve everything all at once, but we can improve one thing at a time, all the time. And that's what this team is doing."

Rhim: "It wasn't insult. I'm just asking if it's the third season now and he's still among the most pressured and hit quarterbacks. I'm just asking you why that is?"

Harbaugh: "I think I answered your question. I can answer it the same way."

Rhim: "You can answer it the same way, but I don't think you answered it."

Harbaugh: "I think I did."

Despite Herbert having his worst statistical season this year, Harbaugh has not wavered in his belief that Herbert is a great quarterback. It's fair to ask why the Chargers can't do more to protect such a great asset, and why this year's Chargers have so far not won any games with him. Even if Harbaugh doesn't like to hear it.

item.title: Monday Night Football: Falcons run over Saints 45-24 to ruin New Orleans' celebration
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson combined for 207 rushing yards and five touchdowns.
item.content:encoded:
The Saints will always have the Hurricane Katrina game on Sept. 25, 2006. Steve Gleason's block of a Falcons' punt is commemorated in a statue outside the Superdome titled "Rebirth."

But Monday night belonged to the Falcons.

Atlanta ruined New Orleans' "Domecoming" celebration, routing the Saints 45-24.

The Superdome cleared out in the second half as the Falcons ran over the Saints, with 205 of their 420 yards coming on the ground. Bijan Robinson had 19 carries for 145 yards and two touchdowns, and Brian Robinson added 14 carries for 62 yards and three touchdowns.

Bijan Robinson went 59 yards for a touchdown on the third play from scrimmage, a foreshadowing of how the night was going to go.

The Falcons led 14-0 at the end of the first quarter and 24-7 at halftime before continuing to pour on the points in the second half.

The Falcons scored the fewest points in the NFL the first two weeks, with 16. In the past two games, since quarterback Michael Penix returned, the Falcons have an NFL-leading 80 points. The Falcons are 2-2 and tied with the Panthers atop the NFC South. The Saints are 1-3.

Penix went 15-of-20 for 223 yards and a touchdown, which was a 31-yard throw to Jahan Dotson. Drake London caught five passes for 96 yards and Dotson had two for 54.

Alvin Kamara turned back time in scoring two of the Saints' touchdowns on runs of 3 and 5 yards. He tied Deuce McAllister's franchise record for most multiple-rushing touchdown games with his 14th.

Late in the fourth quarter, with the game out of reach, Devaughn Vele made one of the best catches of the season. He got both feet down for a 3-yard touchdown with 1:13 left.

Tyler Shough went 30-of-48 for 286 yards and a touchdown despite banging up his left hand. Chris Olave caught eight passes for 116 yards before taking a hard hit on his knee late in the game.

The only bad news for the Falcons was the loss of edge rusher Za'Darius Smith (concussion) and left tackle Jake Matthews (groin). They left in the first half with their injuries and now have a short week to try to get back for the Ravens on Sunday Night Football.

item.title: Seahawks had been planning to use Rashid Shaheed at tailback since training camp
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With the Seahawks thin at running back on Sunday, they deployed receiver Rashid Shaheed in the backfield.
item.content:encoded:
With the Seahawks thin at running back on Sunday, they deployed receiver Rashid Shaheed in the backfield.

He got two carries for 33 yards, including a 28-yard touchdown run.

It wasn't something the Seahawks cooked up this week, with Jadarian Price on injured reserve and Zach Charbonnet still not all the way back from a torn ACL suffered in January.

“We’ve had that in all [training] camp," coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Monday. "This isn’t a quote from [offensive coordinator Brian] Fleury, but felt like it was appropriate because of [Price] going down, he gave us some speed. That was cool.”

Indeed it was. Shaheed's scoring play highlighted his speed and agility in the broken field. He's a player who can make things happen with the ball in his hands. The more the Seahawks can make that happen, the better off they'll be.

Through four games in 2026, Shaheed has seven catches for 73 yards and three carries for 37 yards, plus Sunday's touchdown. He has returned nine punts for 79 yards and 10 kickoffs for 273 yards.

That's fine. But he needs to get the ball more often.

With the Seahawks adding veteran running back Joe Mixon to the practice squad and signing running back Robert Henry Jr. from the Commanders' practice squad, Shaheed may not be part of the running game on Sunday against the 49ers — even if he should be.

item.title: LT Jake Matthews ruled out as Falcons take 31-7 lead
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Falcons left tackle Jake Matthews will not return tonight.
item.content:encoded:
Falcons left tackle Jake Matthews will not return tonight.

The Falcons have ruled him out.

Now, the question becomes: Will his groin injury keep him out of Sunday night's game against the Ravens on a short week?

Matthews has started 199 games in a row, the longest active streak in the NFL. He made his 200th career start on Monday night but left in the first quarter.

The Falcons are rolling in the third quarter, holding a 31-10 lead after Brian Robinson's second rushing touchdown. The Falcons have 173 rushing yards, with Bijan Robinson running for 132 yards and two touchdowns on 16 carries. Brian Robinson has 11 carries for 41 yards.
